Maria — thanks, this is exactly the right place to start. I've attached a MAP draft that maps evaluation milestones to legal/procurement gates and proposes a mitigation path if the DPA extends. High level proposal: 

- Week 0 (Dec 6): Kickoff + access provisioning; host demo schedule.
- Week 1-2 (Dec 6–19): Technical evaluation (sprint tests, latency/cost checks).
- Week 2-3 (Dec 20–Jan 2): Legal review (redlines on DPA).
- Week 3-4 (Jan 3–Jan 16): Procurement sign-off and PO issuance only after DPA agreed.

Mitigation option: we can provision a short 30–90 day isolated pilot environment (data segregation + fenced logs) under a provisional confidentiality addendum so evaluation continues while legal finalizes DPA. If Procurement prefers, we can also run a scoped evaluation limited to synthetic data.

Please see attached: staplepath_map_v1.pdf (MAP draft) and a proposed evidence matrix stub. Questions for you: does Crescent have a hard PO cutoff date we should engineer toward? Also, who should be the single legal point of contact to accept the DPA redline?

If that looks reasonable I'll loop in our Legal/Privacy (Laura) and Solutions (Karthik) to align on the technical and legal guardrails.

Best,

Ben / Maria — thanks for the draft MAP. A couple of legal notes after a quick review: 

1) DPA first: Crescent's procurement policy requires DPA language to be agreed before the PO for any systems processing PHI-adjacent metadata. If Redwood can accept the DPA redline scope (I'll attach comments in a separate doc), procurement may begin PO paperwork in parallel with MSA finalization.
2) Split sign-off: we can accept an MSA with commercial terms while the DPA moves to a short redline cycle, but the order form cannot be executed until DPA terms for data retention and deletion are resolved.
3) Audit evidence: please provide the SOC2 control matrix mapping (not just report) and the retention/encryption policies for the pilot environment.

I'll attach a marked-up redline and an evidence checklist. If Redwood wants a quicker route, we can limit the pilot's scope (non-prod data, isolated VPC) and we will accept a temporary controls attestation for 60 days.
